Alex / Sophie —

Thanks for the materials. I reviewed the draft redlines and left inline comments in the PDF; summary below.

Summary of counsel observations (high level):
- "Named list" carve-in: counsel prefers a two-tier approach — (A) a named list of subprocessors that are "carved in" for operational continuity, and (B) a residual class for "support services" that are limited by purpose and cannot process customer content beyond telemetry/ops. This narrows exposure while keeping runtime ops functional.
- Notice & objection: 30 days' notice with a technical justification for additions is reasonable. Add a short escalation path (CS/Legal) for urgent security-critical additions.
- SCCs + addendum: We can commit to executing SCCs and an EU Addendum; however, language must reflect that for subprocessors located in third countries we rely on SCCs and reasonable safeguards. Counsel flagged a small redline to the standard SCC clause so it doesn't promise impossible contractual obligations (see PDF).
- Evidence: propose a three-tier evidence model in the DPA (SOC2/ISO reports, attestation questionnaire, or self-attestation) mapped to subprocessor criticality.

Proposed execution path: counsel consolidates final redline -> internal legal approval -> Redwood sends DocuSign envelope to DataCorp legal ops. Expect 3 business days for internal sign-off once redline is final.

I'll prepare a cleaned redline with my inline notes removed and send by Mon morning.

Marissa Cole
Director, Legal Programs — Redwood Inference

Sophie / Alex —

Quick technical notes from infra/security that are relevant to the carve-in conversation:

- KMS / Key management: Customers may choose platform-managed or customer-managed keys in some configurations. For carve-in subprocessors that handle encryption or key material, we need a stricter evidentiary bar (SOC2 + specific key handling attestation).
- Retention & logs: We can scope retention limits per account and provide audit logs on request; note that very short retention (e.g., <30 days) can affect performance and caching economics.
- Evidence delivery: I'll attach the subprocessor inventory CSV flagging which vendors have SOC2/ISO and which have security questionnaires on file. For the ones lacking third-party certs, we can provide completed questionnaires within 5 business days.

If DataCorp needs a specific attestation template, share and we'll prioritize.

Rishi Malhotra
Director, Product Infrastructure — Redwood Inference

Thanks — confirming Redwood's operational commitments below so we have a clean record for counsel and procurement:

- Carve-in named list: Redwood will provide an initial named list of carve-in subprocessors by Tue COB (Aug 10) and then publish quarterly updates. Additions will follow 30-day notice plus the right to object with escalation to legal.

- Execution mechanics: Counsel will consolidate and produce a single DocuSign envelope (DPA + EU Addendum) and include a one-page carve-in summary. Expect internal legal sign-off within 3 business days of the final consolidated redline.
